entries.title: Psalms 27:1
segments:
My salvation; Saviour, author of salvation. 
 
Those who have God for their Saviour, Protector, and Guide, have no reason to fear, but may walk through life and through the valley of the shadow of death unmoved by the enemies and dangers that may surround them.

entries.title: Psalms 27:2
segments: Eat up my flesh; destroy me.

entries.title: Psalms 27:3
segments:
In this; even in this situation. 
 
  Be confident; that God will be my salvation.

entries.title: Psalms 27:4
segments: May dwell in the house of the Lord; as one of his household,
.  It is not merely the public worship of God in his sanctuary which the psalmist desires, but also that inward union and communion with God, of which this is the visible earthly embodiment.

entries.title: Psalms 27:5
segments:
His pavilion; where he himself dwells, and where I shall be safe from all the assaults of my foes. 
 
  Secret; hiding-place, as the original word is elsewhere rendered.
God's favor and friendship constitute a more effectual protection than all earthly resources.  The man whose feet God sets upon a rock cannot be cast down by the assaults of his enemies.

entries.title: Psalms 27:6
segments: Though the believer will come off conqueror and more than conqueror over all his foes, yet it will be wholly through the grace of God, and to Him he will give all the glory.

entries.title: Psalms 27:8
segments: Thy face, Lord, will I seek; his inclinations corresponded with his duty.

entries.title: Psalms 27:10
segments:
When my father and my mother forsake me; in times of the most complete desertion.  He mentions father and mother, because they are the last to forsake one. 
 
Though the believer should be forsaken of all earthly friends, and even have not where to lay his head, God will befriend him, provide for him, and bestow upon him all which he needs and which will promote his highest good.

entries.title: Psalms 27:11
segments:
Thy way; the way of thine appointment, the same as the "plain path" mentioned in the next clause.  It is both the way of duty, and the way of divine protection and safety. 
 
  Plain path; that is, as the original denotes, a level path, where there is no danger of stumbling. 
 
The believer who is surrounded by powerful and crafty foes has especial need to pray for divine guidance, that he may be preserved from every false step and kept in the path of duty.

entries.title: Psalms 27:14
segments:
Wait on the Lord; by prayer and supplication, and in the use of all the appointed means of grace. 
 
Waiting upon the Lord in the way of his appointment, his people will renew their strength, will mount up on wings as eagles, run and not be weary, walk and not faint.
